empty: No Harmony hubs found. First set up the “Logitech Harmony Hub” integration in Home Assistant (Settings › Devices & services); the hubs then show up here by themselves.

legend.title: unverified / installed / missing
legend.text: Badges on the Fire TV apps. Unverified means the package name is guessed. After “Read installed apps” it says installed or missing.

legend.title: Favorites
legend.text: Tap keys in edit mode. Chosen keys are collected in the Favorites block, adjustable per activity.

legend.title: Actions
legend.text: Example: name “Candles on”, entity light.candles, action Toggle. The key lights up while the entity is on.

legend.title: Fire TV direct
legend.text: Needs the “Android TV” integration and ADB debugging on the Fire TV. The card then sends keys and starts apps directly, without Harmony.

legend.title: Test connection
legend.text: Sends a harmless command to the Fire TV and shows the answer. No answer usually means ADB debugging is off or the device is in standby.

legend.title: Languages
legend.text: Texts are JSON files in frontend/translations/. To add a language copy a file and translate it, see the README there.

noIntegration: Harmony Deck component not found: settings are not saved.
adbNone: No Android TV / Fire TV entity found. Set up the “Android TV” integration.
adbNoAnswer: no answer (ADB debugging enabled on the Fire TV?)
hintStale: The card ({0}) is older than the integration ({1}). Reload the page so both match.
kbNoLink: not linked to a network device
kbOn: Switching on always goes over Harmony.
helpDirectLegend: Network symbol: the key goes straight to the device, not over Harmony.
netNone: No device is linked to a network device.
actionsHint: Actions are your own buttons: Harmony keys, pauses and Home Assistant entities (lights, scenes, scripts …), alone or as a sequence of several steps. The integration carries them out, also when the page is closed.
actFavsHint: Pick the activity at the top. Below are the devices it uses. Open a device and tick the keys that should appear as favorites in this activity. They come before the device's own favorites.
physFound: Real keyboard detected. Use it for typing?
directReq: Requirements: Fire TV set up in HA via the “Android TV” (ADB) integration, ADB debugging enabled on the Fire TV (Settings › My Fire TV › Developer options), pick its media_player entity. Without it the card uses Harmony keys only.
unvTip: Package name guessed: the Fire TV may not be able to start this app. Check with “Read installed apps” or assign the package yourself.
missTip: This package is not installed on the Fire TV.
pkgNone: No answer. Is the connection reachable and ADB debugging on?
pkgHint: The card asks the Fire TV itself for its apps (like “adb shell pm list packages”). The badges then update and you can assign packages or add your own apps.

tips.skin: Basic look of the card: colours, rounding and key shape.
tips.tileStyle: How the activity tiles at the top look: with icon, icon only or text only.
tips.colorIcons: Colours device and service icons instead of plain grey.
tips.helpNames: Shows device names from the Harmony configuration in the help (“Not working?”).
tips.keyCtl: The browser keyboard controls the running activity: arrow keys, Enter, volume.
tips.vibrate: Short vibration on every key press (phones that support it).
tips.layout: Automatic switches between stacked (narrow) and side by side (wide) depending on the card width.
tips.activeStyle: How the running activity is highlighted: outline with glow, filled tile, or only the icon glows (with the “Text only” tile style the outline is used).
tips.keyStyle: Shape of all keys: as in the chosen look, flat, or classic with shadow.
tips.labels: Small headings above key blocks. Automatic hides them only for the small blocks (Keys, Favorites, Actions).
tips.glow: How a key lights up when pressed.
tips.directEntity: The media_player entity of your Fire TV from the “Android TV” integration. Used for the direct ADB commands.
tips.directDevice: Which Harmony device is this Fire TV. Automatic detects it by name.
tips.directPrefer: Send shared keys (arrows, play …) via Harmony and use ADB only for gaps, or always ADB.
tips.directAct: Also shows the Fire TV keys and apps inside activities, not only in the device.
tips.directModel: Limits the keys to what your model really has.
tips.apps: Which app tiles appear. The badge next to the name shows how far the package name is verified.
tips.actions: Actions are your own keys that switch something in Home Assistant, such as a light, a scene or a script. They work without Harmony and show the state of the entity.
tips.actFavs: Own favorites per activity, shown before the device favorites.
tips.hubVis: Hides this hub in the card.
tips.hubName: Display name in this card only.
tips.collapseHeader: When you open a device or an activity, the header (rooms, status, switch, selection) shrinks to one slim line. Tap it to expand again. With the arrow in the header you can also collapse it by hand, regardless of this setting.
tips.linkTitle: Some devices you do not switch through Harmony but directly in Home Assistant, for example a TV or amplifier with its own integration. A link tells the card that this device belongs to a Harmony activity, so it can compare the two. Without an entity and an activity the link is off.
tips.linkEntity: The Home Assistant device you want to link. Type part of the name or the ID to search.
tips.linkActivity: The Harmony activity that belongs to this device, e.g. TV → “Watch TV”. If the device is on but Harmony shows another activity, a hint with “Match Harmony” appears. It starts this activity.
tips.linkLockActs: Activities ticked here cannot be started while the linked activity runs. That way you do not switch by accident, say in the middle of a film.
tips.linkLockKeys: Key groups ticked here (volume, channel, d-pad, playback) are greyed out while the linked activity runs. Useful when a group does nothing in this activity or does not go through Harmony.
tips.actName: Label of the key, e.g. “Candles on”.
tips.actEntity: What gets switched. Type part of the name or the ID to search.
tips.actOp: What happens on press. Toggle: on if off, off if on (lights, switches). Turn on and turn off: one direction only. Activate: for scenes, scripts and buttons that have no on or off.
tips.actScope: “Always” shows the key in every activity. If you pick an activity, it only appears there.
tips.noBlur: Only for the Frosted glass look. Off: the glass panes stay translucent, but the colour gradient behind is not blurred. Looks flatter, runs smoother and saves battery on weak devices.
tips.jumpRunning: When the card opens it jumps to the room where something is running (activity, Fire TV or a linked device). If several run, the one used last wins. If everything is off you see the default view.
tips.offRelated: Applies to this room. When you switch the Fire TV off with its power key or the red off button, everything the Fire TV activity switches on (e.g. TV, amplifier) goes off too, if the device has a PowerOff command. Devices another running activity needs, and devices hidden in the help, stay on.
tips.helpManual: Some devices are not switched by the hub itself (in the hub: “switch on by hand”). With this switch the help mentions them in one line so you do not forget them.
tips.irVolume: Only while the Fire TV runs without a Harmony activity. Volume up, down and mute then go through the infrared sender of the Cube 3 straight to the TV, without the hub. Only for the model Fire TV Cube.
tips.holdSwitch: While an activity runs, another one only starts when you hold its tile for about a second. Protects against accidents. Without a running activity a tap is enough.
tips.offlineLock: If the Fire TV is linked over ADB but not reachable (unavailable), its activity is greyed out and cannot be started. Standby does not count. No effect without an ADB link.
tips.actTile: Also shows the action as a big tile next to the Harmony activities, where the progress is easy to see.

statusLegend.title: Room icon glows
statusLegend.text: A Harmony activity is running in this room (colour = accent colour of the look).

statusLegend.title: TV with play (Fire TV colour)
statusLegend.text: The Fire TV is playing something. The tooltip names the app.

statusLegend.title: TV (Fire TV colour)
statusLegend.text: The Fire TV is on but not playing.

statusLegend.title: Crossed-out TV, grey
statusLegend.text: The Fire TV is not reachable (asleep or ADB off). Its state is unknown.

statusLegend.title: Chain link
statusLegend.text: The entity of a link runs differently than Harmony reports. “Match Harmony” fixes it.

statusLegend.title: Lock
statusLegend.text: Activity or key is locked while a linked activity runs.

statusHint: Tap a symbol for its explanation.
favEditHint: Pick a device and tap keys to mark them as favorites (star). Favorites per activity are under Settings › Activities.
yamlLock: Set in this card's YAML ({0}: {1}). To release: card › ⋮ › Edit › “Use integration setting”.
yamlHint: Locked because set in the card YAML: {0}. To release: card › ⋮ › Edit, then under “Fixed in this card” click “Use integration setting” (or delete the lines in the YAML code).
holdSwitch: Switching a running activity needs a long press
profIntro: A profile is a named set of settings: look, favourites, icons, hidden activities and actions. All profiles are available to all users. Hub names, Fire TV connection and links are the same for every profile.
profSaveAs: Save current settings as a new profile
profFixedHint: This card is fixed to profile “{0}” (card › ⋮ › Edit › Profile). Switching is locked here.
profAskSave: Save new profile “{0}”? It contains all current settings of “{1}” and is available to all users right away.
profAskRename: Rename profile “{0}”? Cards and users that use it follow automatically.
profAskDelete: Delete profile “{0}”? It disappears for all users and cannot be restored.
profAskDeleteUsers: Assigned to these users (they fall back to automatic): {0}.
profUsersHint: The assigned profile applies automatically when the card has no fixed profile and none was chosen in the browser.

profErr.invalid_name: Please enter a name of 1 to 40 characters.
profErr.unknown_profile: This profile does not exist (any more).

profPersonNote: Only users linked to a person are shown. Technical accounts (e.g. MQTT) stay hidden.
textNone: This device cannot send any of these characters: {0}
helpOff: Help is available once an activity is running
jumpRunning: Jump to the running activity on open
noKeys: This activity has no keys, the device has no commands.
offRelated: Also turn off related devices when switching off
helpManualSet: Mention manually powered devices in the help
lockAppsMoved: Which apps and activities may run despite the lock is set in the security card ("Harmony Deck Security", custom:harmony-deck-security).
favViaDevice: Already a favourite of the device, so it shows up in this activity automatically

cardEditor.title: Fixed in this card
cardEditor.none: Nothing fixed. All settings come from the integration and can be changed in the card's settings mode.
cardEditor.intro: These values are in the card YAML and win over the card's own settings. Any choice in the form above fixes a value.
cardEditor.yamlMode: Note: if the whole dashboard is in YAML mode (file), Home Assistant does not save this change. Then delete the lines in the file by hand.

sec.title: Security
sec.releaseHint: A release pauses the lock for the chosen time. After that, whatever is not allowed is switched off again.
sec.actsHint: Ticked Harmony activities may run despite the lock. Everything else is switched off again after a few seconds.
sec.appsHint: Ticked apps may run despite the lock. The home screen is allowed by default (without it no other app), newly installed apps are blocked. More apps show up after "Read installed apps" or in the list of interventions (with "Allow").
sec.noFire: No Fire TV is connected for this room. Connect it in the main card: settings, tab "Fire TV".
sec.appsNever: The app list has not been read from the device yet.
sec.scheduleHint: In mode "Schedule" the lock only works during these times. If the end is before the start, the window runs over midnight into the next day. Equal times mean the whole day.
sec.scheduleEmpty: No time window yet. Without one, mode "Schedule" never locks.
sec.readOnly: Only administrators can change the lock.
sec.notAvailable: The lock is not available. Is the Harmony Deck integration running (0.3.0 or newer)?
sec.entities: For automations every hub has entities: switch "Lock", select "Lock mode", button "Release", sensor "Lock active".
sec.testHint: Shows what the lock would switch off at this moment. Nothing is switched off.
sec.testOff: The lock does not work at the moment, nothing would be switched off.
sec.testClean: The lock works, and nothing blocked is running.
sec.testHub: The activity “{0}” would be switched off.
sec.testFire: The Fire TV (“{0}”) would be sent to standby.
sec.legendInstalled: = confirmed: installed on the Fire TV or seen before (checked apps are always bright).
sec.offDevHint: Devices that the lock also switches off when it switches off the Fire TV. Meant for devices that the Fire TV switches on itself (for example TV and amplifier by infrared). They get the command PowerOff over the hub, even when no activity runs.
sec.offDevNone: No devices with their own PowerOff command found (or the hub configuration cannot be read).
sec.dbgHint: Real package names from the Fire TV (administrators only). "Read installed apps" above refreshes the list.
sec.dbgNoList: No list yet. Press "Read installed apps" first.
sec.launcherAsk: Without the home screen the Fire TV cannot be used while the lock is on. All other apps are taken off as well. Continue?
sec.launcherOff: Home screen not allowed: while the lock is on the Fire TV is switched off at once. Other apps can only be allowed again once the home screen is checked.

secLockTile: Locked: the lock does not allow this activity
devBackAct: Back to the remote of the activity

tabHints.look: How the card looks: look, tiles and keys. Applies to all rooms of this profile.
tabHints.behave: How the card is operated: tapping, holding, keyboard and what it does by itself. Applies to all rooms of this profile.
tabHints.devs: Own symbols for the devices of this hub.
tabHints.acts: Symbols of the activities, which are shown as tiles, favourites per activity and the link to another entity.
tabHints.misc: Name and visibility of this hub and what happens when switching off.
tabHints.info: Technical details of the hub and the meaning of the symbols.
tabHints.dd: Links a Harmony device to a media player in Home Assistant. The keys still go over infrared through the hub; the media player controls and reports over the network: state, volume level and source.

adbHelp: Fire TV not reachable. Check: Fire TV switched on and on the network? ADB debugging on (Settings › My Fire TV › Developer options)? Reload the “Android TV” integration in Home Assistant. Then “Test connection”.
hideEditHint: Tap keys that should no longer appear for this device (eye). They disappear in the device view and in the remotes of the activities. This is not the lock: tap again to bring them back.
actTile: Show as a tile in the activity list
stepsNone: No steps yet. Add the first one below.

stepTypeHints.key: Send a key of a device
stepTypeHints.irvol: Bring an infrared device to a volume
stepTypeHints.dev: Switch a device over the network, set volume or source

actErrSteps: At least one step is needed.
actBusy: Another action is running on this hub.
stepMore: More matches: please search more precisely.
stepPauseType: Tap to type an exact value
actFavHint: Keys of any devices; they appear under the opened action.
valHint: Only switched-on values are sent; everything else stays as it is. What the device cannot do does not appear here.
valWhiteOrColor: White or colour, not both – Home Assistant wants it that way.
valSourceNone: The device reports no sources right now. The list appears when it is on.
irvHint: For devices controlled by infrared only. Harmony Deck first presses "down" until the device is surely at 0, then "up" to the level. If the device is muted, it may stay muted, depending on the device.
irvNoDevices: No device of this hub has keys for volume up and down.
irvDuration: Takes about {0} s ({1}× down, then {2}× up).
irvSetupHint: If the device misses presses, make the time longer.
volumeCapHint: For media players in actions: a step may not set it louder.
cPickWait: What should be waited for? Choose an entity.
cPickIf: What should be checked? Choose an entity.
ddHint: Pick the media player for each device. The cog opens the device page.
ddCanNot: Reports no capabilities (off or not reachable).
ddVolDirect: Set volume directly instead of via IR
ddVolDirectHint: The step "Volume (IR)" then sets the value on the device instead of counting down first and then up.
devHint: Only devices linked under Settings → Network control appear here.
devNoDevices: No device linked yet. Do that under Settings → Network control.
devSourceUnknown: The device reports no source list: type the name exactly.
mmShouldOn: {0}: should be on but is off.
mmShouldOff: {0}: should be off but is on.
ddInputsHint: Which source of the media player belongs to which Harmony input? Without a choice Harmony Deck guesses by the names. After that the card tells you when the TV is on a different input.
ddVolVia: In {0} the volume goes through "{1}", not through this device.

ddQuirks.source_is_channel_list: The source list in Home Assistant is the channel list, not the HDMI inputs. The input check stays silent here.
ddQuirks.mute_toggle_only: Mute can only be toggled. Harmony Deck checks the state first and switches only when needed.
ddQuirks.no_power_on: Switching on is not set up in Home Assistant (for Netcast: the integration's "turn on" action). Switching off works.
ddQuirks.volume_on_release: Volume is set when the slider is released (this TV reacts slowly).

ddSourcesSeen: Last seen – the device only reports its inputs while it is on
ddRescanOff: The device is off, so there is little to read. Switch it on and press again.
ddRescanHint: Forgets the remembered values and reads capabilities and inputs from the device now (best with the device switched on).
preferHint: Via Harmony the keys can arrive late or not at all (the hub sends infrared or Bluetooth). Direct ADB is fast; it is the default for a new setup.
